text:
Roman Kantserov came over from the KHL, where he scored 64 points for Magnitogorsk last season, and has become the one thing going steadily right in Chicago. The 22-year-old rookie has 9 goals in 19 games and a nine-game point streak (6 goals, 3 assists) through a stretch when the Blackhawks lost six straight.

The finishing will cool. He is shooting 28% and has 9 goals on 4.7 expected, nearly double what his chances suggest. Our range for his shooting sits nearer 15%.

The bigger worry is the five-on-five picture. Chicago gets only 38.8% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and his teammates have scored 3.8 fewer goals than their chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, through eight games, sees nothing far from a typical forward yet.

History says he is already ahead of schedule: among forwards picked 34th to 54th overall since 2005, the median first full season was 0.30 points a game. He is at 0.63. Our projection has him finishing between 20 and 34 goals. What to watch: whether he starts creating more of his own chances.
